pr.title: Count a drawer's actions down from 9, and ask before a dismiss
pr.head: 1767d45e3ca01cbd26a54206e0724a9b85e033fd

summary: Projector's band is a panel above the Claude Code prompt that lists your pull requests and your agents' questions and notices. Pressing an item's line opens its drawer: the item's detail, a question's options, and action lines such as discuss, dismiss, and snooze. Options already took the digits 1 to 6, which work both while the band holds the keyboard and when typed first into an empty prompt. The actions took the letters d, x, and s, which work only from the band.

This pull request gives the actions digits too, counting down from 9: 7 discusses, 8 dismisses or restores, and 9 snoozes or unsnoozes. A digit that works from the prompt makes a stray dismiss easy, so dismiss now asks first: 8: yes, dismiss question and 9: no, keep it. While snooze asks how long, its four lengths take 1 to 4 in place of the hidden options, with 9: cancel.

One atom, bandAsked, records which question an open drawer is asking, replacing bandSnoozing. An atom is a small piece of state the Claude Code plugin engine keeps and redraws the band from. The band forgets the question when the drawer closes or the question is answered, forgets either question once the item is resolved anywhere, and forgets the snooze question once the item is snoozed.

The open item's own line also changes. It drops its - bullet, so the engine's 0: takes its place, and it is no longer inverted, though it keeps the item's color. In a terminal it becomes the band's top bar while the divider steps aside: a rule in the default color runs from the subject to the pull request and age. The drawer is indented by the width of 0: , so its lines start under the item's text.

Two smaller changes to the band's look: an open notice's line is drawn in the theme's inactive gray, apart from the subtle of resolved and snoozed items, and the divider ends with the reload's age in the rows' short form, such as 12s, with the counts after a leading ─.

cards.title: Which digit does what in an open drawer
cards.html:
Drawer showsDigits
Actions0 closes, 1–6 options, 7 discuss, 8 dismiss or restore, 9 snooze or unsnooze
Dismiss confirmation0, options 1–6, 8 yes, 9 keep it
Snooze lengths0, 1–4 lengths, 9 cancel; options hidden
Pull request7 discuss PR, 8 dismiss PR, then 8 yes or 9 keep it

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review found that restoring an item dismissed elsewhere brought back a stale dismiss confirmation, so the next 8 dismissed without asking. Fixed: restore clears the question, and forgetAsked clears it once the item is resolved. That thread is resolved.
  • The review of aaa7e46 suggested keeping a dismiss confirmation on a snoozed item, and 9f010c0 does so.
  • The reviews of 9f010c0 and 1767d45 are clean. Both ask one question: the open line's rule counts the subject in code points, so a subject with emoji or CJK characters, which draw two cells wide, may overflow the row.
  • The type check could not run, so nothing here confirms that the engine's color type accepts inactive.
  • The user has tried the digits from an empty prompt in a live session and kept that behavior.

groups.title: The drawer's digits and its two questions
groups.kicker: How the band draws action lines, the confirmation, and the snooze lengths
intro: All drawer lines now draw through one helper, drawLines, which renders a plain Button with a digit before its label, as 7: discuss question. The action lines, the dismiss confirmation, and the snooze lengths are three lists of the same Line shape, and the drawer picks one of them by what bandAsked holds.

bandAsked is null, or names the open drawer and whether it asks how long to snooze or whether to dismiss. Pressing dismiss or snooze sets it. Picking a length, confirming, keeping, cancelling, restoring, opening or closing a drawer, and anything that closes the drawer through closeDrawer clear it. forgetAsked also clears it when a store read or an action shows the item resolved, and clears the snooze question when it shows the item snoozed.

The open item's line, at the top of its drawer, has no bullet and no inverse, and keeps the item's color. In a terminal a rule follows the subject to the row's end, as the divider's rule does. DRAWER_INDENT, the width of the 0: the engine draws before that line, indents the drawer under the item's text.

The divider, the rule at the top of the band, now opens with ─ and the counts of open questions and notices, and ends with the reload's age, such as 12s, in subtle. Its rule fills the space between, so the row still ends at bodyColumns, where the engine draws [-]. An open notice's line takes NOTICE_COLOR, the theme's inactive gray.

checks.text: The confirmation and the length lines replace lines in place, so a digit from the prompt presses whatever line holds that digit now. That is why dismiss asks on 8 and confirms on 8: a deliberate dismiss is 8 8, and a single stray 8 only asks.

files.note: Replaces the letters with digits, adds the dismiss confirmation for items and pull requests, draws the snooze lengths as keyed lines in the options' place, forgets a stale question, redraws the open item's line with a rule after it, grays open notices, and ends the divider with the reload's age.

checks.text: inactive is a Claude Code theme key. The tests check only the prop the band passes, and the type check could not run, so whether the engine accepts the key rests on the owner's preview.
DRAWER_INDENT is computed from CLOSE_HOTKEY, so the indent follows the close key if it ever changes.

forgetAsked runs from replace after each band action and from setItems after each store read. A resolved item clears either question. A snoozed item clears only the snooze question, because a snoozed item can still be dismissed.
ask(key, null) clears the question whatever drawer it names. closeDrawer is the narrower path: it clears the question only when it belongs to the drawer being closed.
The divider ends at bodyColumns: the lead ─ <counts> , then enough ─ to leave room for <age>. Traced with and without counts and a time, and the tests check the divider's length.

No digit is shared in a drawer. inbox.check caps a question at six choices, so options use at most 1–6. The lengths use 1–4 only while the options are hidden. The actions, the confirmation, and cancel use 7–9. Traced through each state and confirmed by the digitsOf assertions in hooks/band.test.tsx, which pass.

The rule ends the row at bodyColumns. The row is 0: , the subject, a space and the rule, then sending, the pull request, and the age column, each after a one-column gap, and notesWidth counts each note with its gap. Traced against the row's JSX, and the new test checks the sum.

The subject is measured in code points, but an emoji or a CJK character draws two cells wide. A subject with such characters asks for a rule wider than the row has room for. Whether the engine clips the overflow or wraps it onto a second row is unchecked, because the tests do no layout.
A pull request's drawer gets the same confirmation, with yes, dismiss PR. Dismissing a pull request stops every loop of this session that tracks it.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Every dismiss in the suite now confirms, plus tests that pin the new keys, the forgotten question, the open line, the divider, and the colors
intro: Each existing test that dismisses an item or a pull request now presses confirm:<id> after dismiss:<id>. New tests pin the action digits and labels, the dismiss confirmation with its ring moves, the snooze lengths on 1 to 4, a question forgotten once its item is dismissed or snoozed from a terminal, a snoozed item's dismiss confirmation that stands, and the open line's rule. Existing tests now check the open line's colors, the notice gray, the drawer's indent, and the divider's new shape.
